metadata.title: SOPP 8203 Administrative Processing and Review Management of Charging Requests (Cost Recovery Requests) for Investigational New Drugs and Investigational Devices
metadata.edition: 8203 · listed on the FDA SOPP page, 2026-11-26
metadata.legal_basis: CBER Standard Operating Procedure and Policy (internal FDA procedure). Informative; not binding on applicants.

candidates.statement: 1. IDE regulations allow sponsors to charge for an investigational device, however, the charge cannot exceed an amount necessary to recover the costs of manufacture, research, development, and handling of the investigational device (21 CFR 812.7(b)). A sponsor must justify the proposed charges for the device in the IDE application, state the amount to be charged, and explain why the charge does not constitute commercialization (21 CFR 812.20(b)(8)). The informed consent must include a description of any additional costs to the subject that may result from participation in the research (21 CFR 50.25(b)(3)).
candidates.context: 2. Likewise, as noted in the preamble (45 FR 3751) to these regulations, finalized in 1980, the FDA/CBER is implicitly empowered to determine

candidates.statement: whether the charge sought by the IDE sponsor is “excessive”. The preamble (45 FR 3751) suggests FDA/CBER staff should understand device market realities but also remain cognizant of ethical considerations, stating that “[m]any devices, unlike most drugs, are expensive to manufacture, and it is unrealistic to prohibit a sponsor from recovering costs. It is a well-established ethical principle, however, that no profit should be made on experimental devices.

candidates.statement: 1. Charging request: a. In accordance with 21 CFR 312.8(a), an IND sponsor who wishes to charge for investigational drugs under an IND, including investigational use of its approved drug, must seek FDA’s prior authorization by submitting a charging request to FDA, with the following exceptions:
candidates.context: A. Policy for Charging INDs i. Sponsors do not need to obtain FDA authorization to charge for an approved drug obtained from another entity not affiliated with the sponsor for use as part of the clinical trial evaluation (e.g., in a clinical trial of a new use of the approved drug, for use of the approved drug as an active control, or as concomitant therapy) (21 CFR 312.8(a)(1)).

candidates.statement: Note: FDA interprets § 312.8(d)(2) as permitting the sponsor to recover the cost of the fees paid to a third party for administering an intermediate-size patient population or treatment IND or protocol, including any profit for the third party that may be included in the fees. The fees paid to the third party should be included in the calculation for cost recovery that the sponsor provides in its request to charge. In addition, FDA recommends that the sponsor disclose to the patients any relationship it may have with the third party (See FDA’s Guidance for Industry : Charging for Investigational Drugs Under an IND, Questions and Answers Q18).
candidates.context: b) For an expanded access IND under 21 CFR 312.315 (intermediate- size patient populations) and 21 CFR 312.320 (large patient populations), in addition to the direct costs described in 21 CFR 312.8(d)(1)(i), a sponsor may recover the costs of monitoring the expanded access IND or protocol, complying with IND reporting requirements, and other administrative costs directly associated with the expanded access IND (21 CFR 312.8(d)(2)). c) Per 21 CFR 312.8(d)(3), supporting documentation for cost recovery calculation must be provided to show that the calculation is consistent with the requirements of 21 CFR 312.8(d)(1) and if applicable 21 CFR 312.8(d)(2). The documentation must be accompanied by a statement that an independent certified public accountant has reviewed and approved the calculations.

candidates.statement: c) Per 21 CFR 312.8(d)(3), supporting documentation for cost recovery calculation must be provided to show that the calculation is consistent with the requirements of 21 CFR 312.8(d)(1) and if applicable 21 CFR 312.8(d)(2). The documentation must be accompanied by a statement that an independent certified public accountant has reviewed and approved the calculations.

candidates.statement: Note: When the amount to be charged for a drug is simply the amount charged to the expanded access sponsor by a third party who provides the drug to the expanded access sponsor, such that there is no calculation of cost made by the sponsor to which the requirement under § 312.8(d)(3) applies, the expanded access sponsor should provide a copy of the receipt or invoice from the source that provided the drug to the expanded access sponsor to justify the amount to be charged for the drug (see FDA’s Guidance for Industry: Charging for Investigational Drugs Under an IND, Questions and Answers Q13 & Q21) iii. Specify that the charge is limited to the number of patients authorized to receive the drug under the treatment use, if there is a limitation.

The documentation must be accompanied by a statement that an independent certified public accountant has reviewed and approved the calculations. iv. Provide the intended duration for the charge. Demonstrate the understanding that unless FDA specifies a shorter period, charging for expanded access to an investigational drug may continue for 1 year from the time of FDA authorization per 21 CFR 312.8(c)(4)).

If a sponsor for expanded access use wishes to continue charging beyond the authorized duration, the sponsor must submit an IND amendment to FDA to request reauthorization. FDA recommends that the sponsor submit a request to reauthorize charging at least 60 days prior to the expiration of the existing authorization. The sponsor must receive written reauthorization from FDA before it can continue to charge for the investigational drug beyond the period previously authorized.

Sponsors must notify FDA of changes to an authorized charge, including any requests to increase charges, through an information amendment (21 CFR 312.31). 2. FDA Review & Authorization a. There is no statutory requirement on the time frame for FDA to respond to a charge request for INDs. CBER intends to respond to charge requests within 30 days of receipt when possible.

candidates.statement: 4. Recordkeeping and Record Retention a. Sponsors must comply with documentation requirements specified in 21 CFR 312, including 21 CFR 312.8 and 21 CFR 312.57.
candidates.context: b. When reviewing sponsor requests to reauthorize charging, CBER will ensure that the sponsor’s justification for charging continues to meet the requirements stated in 21 CFR 312.8, and that the sponsor continues to make good faith progress toward FDA/CBER’s marketing approval for the product under investigation. 5. Withdrawal: a. FDA will withdraw authorization to charge if it determines that charging is interfering with the development of a drug for marketing approval or that the criteria for the authorization are no longer being met per 21 CFR 312.8(a)(4) (e.g., A small company or academic sponsor were acquired by a much larger company, it may no longer face “extraordinary circumstances” requiring cost recovery for its product during a clinical study and CBER may then reconsider its cost recovery authorization).

candidates.statement: 2. If the device is to be sold, the sponsor shall include in the IDE application the amount to be charged and an explanation of why sale does not constitute commercialization of the device within the IDE application per 21 CFR 812.20(b)(8). For IDE for treatment use, if the device is to be sold, the sponsor must include in the IDE application, the price to be charged and a statement indicating that the price is based on manufacturing and handling costs only per 21 CFR 812.36(c)(1)(x).
